Title: Server-Side JS Code Injection (RCE) via eval in contributions handler
Analysis:
In `app/routes/contributions.js`, the method `handleContributionsUpdate` processes the input parameters `req.body.preTax`, `req.body.afterTax`, and `req.body.roth` using the highly insecure global JavaScript `eval()` function: `const preTax = eval(req.body.preTax)`. Since these request body variables come directly from untrusted user input without any validation or sanitization before reaching the `eval` sink, this permits Server-Side JavaScript Code Injection / Remote Code Execution (RCE).

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
`POST /contributions`
Body: `preTax=require('child_process').execSync('id').toString()&afterTax=1&roth=1`
This will execute the command `id` on the server hosting the Node.js application.

Title: NoSQL Injection in allocations-dao.js via threshold parameter
Analysis:
The application takes the `threshold` parameter from `req.query` (the URL query string) in `app/routes/allocations.js`, which is passed to `allocationsDAO.getByUserIdAndThreshold`. Inside `getByUserIdAndThreshold`, the `searchCriteria` constructs a `$where` query using string interpolation with the unsanitized `threshold` value: `this.userId == ${parsedUserId} && this.stocks > '${threshold}'`. An attacker can supply a malicious string containing a single quote to break out of the string literal and execute arbitrary Javascript code on the MongoDB database server (NoSQL Injection/Server-side JavaScript Injection).

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
`GET /allocations/123?threshold=1%27%3B+while(true)%7B%7D%27` or `GET /allocations/123?threshold=1%27%20%7C%7C%201%3D%3D1%20%7C%7C%20%27`

Title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in Research handler
Analysis:
In `app/routes/research.js`, the `displayResearch` method retrieves `url` and `symbol` from `req.query`. It concatenates them as `const url = req.query.url + req.query.symbol` and then performs a GET request using the `needle` HTTP client: `needle.get(url, ...)`. Since there is no validation or sanitization on the `url` parameter, an attacker can specify an arbitrary URL (including internal services, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:27017` or `http://169.254.169.254`), making the application vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). Additionally, because the response `body` is directly written back to the user response via `res.write(body)` with `Content-Type: text/html`, it also acts as an arbitrary proxy or a reflected XSS sink.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
`GET /research?url=http://127.0.0.1:27017/&symbol=test`
or
`GET /research?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/&symbol=`

Title: Missing Authorization (Broken Function Level Access Control) on Benefits route
Analysis:
The routes `/benefits` (GET and POST) are protected only by the `isLoggedIn` middleware in `app/routes/index.js`, which checks if the user is authenticated but not whether they are an administrator. Inside `BenefitsHandler`, the code lists and modifies benefits for other non-admin users assuming the requester is an admin (e.g., hardcoding `user: { isAdmin: true }` in the render template data). Any logged-in non-admin user can access the `/benefits` page and update start dates/benefits of any user (Broken Function Level Access Control / Missing Authorization).

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A regular user logs in and sends:
`GET /benefits`
Or sends a POST request:
`POST /benefits` with body: `userId=1&benefitStartDate=2026-09-01`

Title: Global Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Disabled Autoescape in Swig
Analysis:
The templating system Swig has its autoescape feature explicitly set to `false` in `server.js`. This is a classic vulnerability leading to stored and reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) across multiple pages of the application because any variables rendered into templates (like the user profile's name, address, website, or memos) will not be HTML-escaped by default.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Setting a user's address or first name to `<script>alert('XSS')</script>` will execute JavaScript in the browser of any user who views that profile.

Title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in allocations route
Analysis:
The application allows a logged-in user to access the allocations page of any user via `/allocations/:userId`. In `app/routes/allocations.js`, the code extracts `userId` from `req.params` (the URL path parameter) rather than checking the logged-in user's session (`req.session.userId`). This allows an authenticated attacker to view or retrieve the allocations of any other user in the database simply by guessing or iterating their `userId` (IDOR / Insecure Direct Object Reference).

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
`GET /allocations/1` (when the attacker's actual userId in session is `2`).

Title: Open Redirect via learn route
Analysis:
In `app/routes/index.js`, the `/learn` route takes a URL from the query string `req.query.url` and redirects the user directly to it using `res.redirect(req.query.url)` without validating that the target URL belongs to a trusted domain. This allows attackers to craft open redirect links that can be used in phishing campaigns.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
`GET /learn?url=http://malicious-website.com`
